first:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: a finished editorial illustration in the preface of the Chinese university textbook “AI 开源通识（AtomGit 版）”.
Primary request: “打开，才能理解” — opening a real open-source project lets the learner inspect supporting materials, without pretending that everything inside AI is revealed.
Create an intelligent, professional hand-drawn science-publishing illustration with a clear visual metaphor, warm and quietly playful. Landscape 3:2, high-resolution, suitable for full-column book printing and a phone screen.
Composition: an oversized realistically constructed accordion-bound project folio lies partly open on a warm ivory desk, seen from a low three-quarter viewpoint. From its open folds, ordinary tangible project materials emerge: a simple README sheet, a source-file sheet with only a few abstract code-like strokes, a small usage-note booklet, and a coral pencil. A large real handheld magnifying glass resting diagonally over a citation marker and a paperclip enlarges that one small piece of evidence. On one side, a translucent smooth speech-bubble-shaped paper silhouette suggests a fluent AI answer; the reader's attention travels into the opened material rather than a magical machine. A couple of the folio's far pages remain folded, suggesting limits to what is known. No arrows, no exact technical architecture. The key subject should remain understandable at small size.
Medium: fine graphite and dark-ink drawing, visible but restrained pencil hatching, hand-painted gouache washes, selective tactile paper-cut collage depth. Ground the objects in plausible real stationery and bookbinding. Keep plenty of breathing space. Mature contemporary textbook editorial art, not an icon diagram and not a children's cartoon.
Palette: warm paper #F6F3EB, deep ink #1D2433, restrained indigo #5146D9, coral #F27A59, tiny teal #3F958D. Gentle natural daylight, mostly matte surfaces. No gradients as the dominant style.
Text: only one small readable “README” on the first sheet. No other words, letters, numerals, titles, captions or figure numbers in the artwork. Captions will be typeset outside.
Constraints: no robots, no brain circuits, no glowing neural networks, no humanoid AI, no fake product interface, no invented logos, no claims of fully open training data, no exact scientific schematic. No busy stars, badges or visual clutter. No hard frame. Entire composition within the canvas. Artwork must feel calm, insightful, grounded and beautiful.
first_revision:
Edit this illustration for a serious university textbook about AI open-source projects. Keep the excellent hand-drawn watercolor-and-pencil rendering, accordion folio, README sheet, dark code-stroke sheet, magnifying glass over citation marker, coral pencil, warm paper and indigo palette, viewpoint and approximate composition.
Make one targeted content correction: remove ALL landscape scenery, travel postcards and botanical illustrations ON the project documents, including the lower-right loose postcards. Replace those document pictures with simple, carefully drawn, unlabelled geometric sketches of files, speech bubbles, a small branching project-folder tree, and the outline of a plain laptop. The notebook should show a small document-and-magnifier sketch, not a landscape. These are symbolic sketches, not fake software screenshots or exact technical diagrams.
Reduce distracting foreground plants, retaining only a tiny background glimpse if necessary. Keep the overall quiet natural studio light. Do not add robot, brain, neural-network, neon, magical engine, arrows or busy symbols. No text except the existing correctly spelled README. Do not add figure numbers or captions. Preserve all key real physical stationery objects and the idea that some far pages remain folded. Final image: professional thoughtful technology-publishing illustration, visually grounded in a real study desk, no longer resembling a travel scrapbook.
second:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: second preface illustration for a university textbook about understanding AI through open-source projects and contributing useful work with AI.
Create an intellectually clear, professional hand-drawn editorial illustration, landscape 3:2, high resolution.
Visual idea: a useful work grows through checking, human annotations and sharing. Show a TOP-DOWN worktable, an entirely different composition from an open book or standing folio. Three large real sheets of paper form a loose triangular arrangement with generous warm ivory negative space between them: at upper left an early draft with short abstract text strokes and a simple geometric project-guide thumbnail; at lower center a working copy with a CORAL pencil held by one realistic human hand, a few cross-outs and one circled question mark, plus a modest source note attached with a real paperclip; at right an improved copy with a clearer arrangement and source markers, being gently passed by a second person's hand toward a third hand just entering the right edge. A small transparent tracing-paper note overlaps the improved copy, suggesting another reader can add to it. One indigo notebook at the extreme left edge, a thin teal pencil, three sticky tabs, otherwise no clutter.
Communicate continued improvement and human judgment, NOT an automatic pipeline, not a perfect final result, not a scored assessment. No arrows, no UI, no precise data, no fake testimony. The hands are only hands, natural anatomy, differentiated sleeves, no character portraits.
Style: loose yet accurate graphite and ink contours, visible light crosshatching, restrained gouache/risograph-like color, subtle paper texture, editorial collage. NOT photorealistic. Mostly calm blank paper, limited indigo #5146D9, muted teal #3F958D, coral #F27A59 accents, dark ink #1D2433. Background exactly warm paper-family #F6F3EB. Preserve a generous clean outer margin. Contemporary science-publishing illustration, sophisticated, warm and engaging.
Text: no words, letters or numerals anywhere. Abstract text strokes and a single question mark are enough. Captions and the exact worked example will be typeset outside this picture.
Avoid: plants, mountains, travel photographs, cups, decorative stars, robots, circuit brains, lightbulbs, trophy badges, large titles, labels, rainbow colors, charts, tiny interface elements. The illustrations should help a reader understand that the change between drafts and the reasons for those changes are part of the work.
